title: R’ Abba bar Yosef
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Beitzah, chapter 1, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Beitzah.1.3.3): R’ Yose son of R’ Bun said that R’ Zeira [ר״ז] and R’ Abba bar Yosef disagreed. Hyman identifies him as Rava, citing [Beitzah 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.8b.11), and says he is mentioned under this name only once. Hyman explains this by saying that R’ Yose son of R’ Bun went down to Babylonia for a short time and, when he returned, brought this halakhah with him in Rava’s name; see his entry. We also find R’ Abba bar Yosef in [Yalkut, Samuel I, remez 77](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.77.5), but the statement appears in [Midrash Shmuel 1:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Shmuel.1.7) as a teaching that R’ Abba bar Marya gave in R’ Yitzchak’s name. Hyman calls the [Sanhedrin, chapter 4, halakhah 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.4.8.2) reading, “R’ Abba bar Yasa in the name of R’ Yohanan,” a scribal error and says it should read as the statement appears there in [chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.1.4.2): “R’ Abba, R’ Yasa, in the name of R’ Yohanan.” He explains that R’ Abba and R’ Yasa both said it in R’ Yohanan’s name.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The linked Yerushalmi names Abba bar Yosef with Zeira. The Bavli names Yose bar Chama or, in the alternative, Rava son of Rav Yosef bar Chama. Hyman’s identification, itinerary and “only once” claim belong to his reconstruction.
The linked Yalkut has Abba bar Yosef speaking in Yitzchak’s name. The consulted Midrash Shmuel gives Abba bar Madya, beside Hyman’s Marya.

The linked Hebrew of Sanhedrin 4:8 reads Ba bar Yasa in Yochanan’s name. Sanhedrin 1:4 names Ba and Yasa separately. Guggenheimer’s translation of 4:8 follows the latter reading. Hyman’s chapter 1 label ד״הד is irregular.
